content.outcome: Make canonical kis-mcp-doc development and verification use a locally installed, Authenticode-valid CPython instead of uv-managed CPython, while retaining uv for deterministic dependency management.

classification.reason: The change alters runtime selection at the repository verification boundary and must preserve Windows security controls.

authority_model: Windows security policy remains enabled and is not weakened.
The repository runtime policy is machine-readable and contains no machine-specific absolute interpreter path.
uv remains the lock/sync tool but may not select or download a managed Python for canonical local verification.
requirements: R1: Canonical verification MUST use a non-uv-managed CPython runtime on Windows.
R2: The selected CPython executable MUST have a valid Authenticode signature from the configured trusted publisher.
R3: Runtime discovery MUST be machine-portable and MUST NOT commit a user-specific Python path.
R4: uv dependency synchronization MUST disable managed-Python selection and automatic Python downloads.
R5: Verification MUST fail closed when no compliant interpreter is available.
R6: The design MUST be reusable as a pilot pattern for later governed KIS/tool-user rollout without changing parent KIS authority in this change.
R7: The implementation MUST NOT add Defender exclusions, Smart App Control bypasses, execution-policy weakening, or writes outside C:/Projects.
implementation_plan: P1: Add a machine-readable Windows runtime policy.
P2: Add a PowerShell preflight that discovers and validates a signed system CPython.
P3: Bind canonical verification to the validated runtime and disable uv-managed Python/downloads.
P4: Add tests for policy and verification integration.
P5: Run canonical verification and correlate fresh Code Integrity events.
verification_criteria: V1: runtime-preflight resolves the installed Python Software Foundation CPython 3.11 runtime and rejects uv-managed candidates.
V2: a fresh worktree environment is synchronized by uv using that runtime.
V4: no new Code Integrity 3033/3077 block event attributable to the canonical verification workload appears after the test start time.

tasks.text: Establish baseline and identify uv-managed CPython _elementtree.pyd as the current Code Integrity block.
Implement signed-system-Python runtime policy and preflight.
Verify, review, publish, merge, and reconcile.

risks: Publisher matching that is too strict could reject a future valid Python signing certificate.
A clean interpreter can still load a later third-party native extension that violates Code Integrity policy; verification must detect this separately.
explicit_exclusions: Rolling the pattern out to other tool users before this pilot is proven.
